about: scripts/ergotests: runs the Ergo tests of Ergo packages at check time, for the gate and the mutant runner (ST-0).

mutants.name: ergotests-skip-is-pass
mutants.rule: A skipped or incomplete Ergo test fails the run: a skip is not a pass.

mutants.name: ergotests-run-ignored
mutants.rule: -run judges only the obligations it selects: a mutant runner's killer is one test, not its package.

mutants.name: ergotests-empty-run-passes
mutants.rule: A -run that selects no test or law fails: a killer whose test is gone kills nothing silently otherwise.

mutants.name: ergotests-testdata-walked
mutants.rule: DIR/... skips testdata, as the go command does: fixtures there are no packages.

mutants.name: lawkiller-skipped-law-kills
mutants.rule: A killer law must pass outright: one skipped or incomplete at check time kills nothing, so it is no baseline.

mutants.name: lawkiller-law-name-ignored
mutants.from: match := func(r string) bool { return r == "law "+law || strings.HasPrefix(r, "law "+law+" for ") }
mutants.to: match := func(r string) bool { return law != "" && strings.HasPrefix(r, "law ") }
mutants.rule: -killer law:L runs the law L (and its runs for each provider), not every law.

mutants.name: lawkiller-test-matches-law
mutants.rule: -killer NAME names a test; a law is named law:L.

mutants.name: lawkiller-undecided-trusted
mutants.rule: A killer law check time leaves undecided is decided by ergo test --law; trusted as passed, a refutation there kills nothing.

mutants.name: lawkiller-ergo-skip-trusted
mutants.rule: A law ergo test skips kills nothing, so it fails as a killer's baseline.

mutants.name: stdlaw-std-as-folder
mutants.to: if rel, ok := stdPath(abs); false && ok {
mutants.rule: A std package's law runs in-package, as std is checked: checked as a folder, std/json fails S108 and its laws run nowhere (#162).

mutants.name: stdlaw-undecided-std-asks-ergo
mutants.rule: A std law check time leaves undecided is no killer: ergo test cannot check a std folder, so it is not asked.
